name: Himālaya
desc: The snow mountains of the north, home of the gods. Arjuna goes there to win divine weapons; the Pāṇḍavas will make their last walk there.

name: Kāmyaka & Dvaita Forests
desc: Kāmyaka and Dvaitavana, the forests near the Sarasvatī where the Pāṇḍavas spend twelve years of exile.

name: Matsya · Upaplavya
desc: King Virāṭa’s kingdom, where the Pāṇḍavas hide in their thirteenth year. Its town Upaplavya becomes their base for the war.

name: Dvārakā
desc: Kṛṣṇa’s city on the western sea, capital of the Yādavas.

name: Mount Mahendra
desc: Paraśurāma’s retreat on Mount Mahendra, where Karṇa studied in disguise as a brahmin.

name: Gaṅgā’s Bank
desc: The Gaṅgā near Hastināpura, where Karṇa offers worship to the sun each day — and where no one who asks him for a gift is refused.

name: Inner Palace, Hastināpura
desc: The private quarters of the blind king Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Queen Gāndhārī.

name: Assembly Hall, Hastināpura
desc: The royal assembly of the Kurus in Hastināpura: the throne, the elders, the court.

name: Pāṇḍava Camp
desc: The tents of the Pāṇḍava army at the edge of the battlefield.

name: Kurukṣetra
desc: The plain of Kurukṣetra, ‘the field of dharma’, where eighteen armies meet for eighteen days.

name: Dvaipāyana Lake
desc: Dvaipāyana lake, where Duryodhana hides on the last day of the war.

name: Kaurava Camp
desc: The tents of the Kaurava army across the field.
